name: agent-fs-permission-grants
body:
The agent-grant surface for the fs tools: the `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md` template rules that generate each code-writer's `permissions` array with `apg_rm` / `apg_mv` / `apg_cp` granted deny-by-default (the tools' CALLABILITY gate) and the path globs the tools self-enforce (the `edit`-action effective scope: allow rules grant, deny rules revoke, the LAST match wins). Rule 6 carries the fs-tool grants rather than a bash filesystem grant; rule 10 treats path-scoped fs-tool globs as their own scope, distinct from cwd-agnostic shell patterns. For a code-writer (`requirements.requirement.code-writer-worktree-only-writes`) those globs are granted WORKTREE-ONLY (`apg/.worktrees/*/<glob>`), anchored away from the repo root — opencode resolves globs against the session workspace root (the main checkout), so a repo-root grant reaches main, while the worktree form reaches the worktree. Rule 6 and rule 10 state so consistently. The tools read the whole `edit` rule set including `deny` entries, so the template's sibling cross-denial (`deny a sibling's apg/.worktrees/*/src/golib/**`) is honoured by the fs tools exactly as `edit` honours it (`requirements.note.fs-scope-deny-mirror`) — rule 10's parenthetical describes the scope as the effective allow-plus-deny set rather than ""the allow globs"" alone.

Product source in `solution.container.opencode-suite`; the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts.

implemented-by: `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`.
